claim: Deleting Kindlin-2 expression in hepatocytes using Alb-Cre transgenic mice causes severe inflammation resulting in premature death.
source: Here we show that deleting the focal adhesion protein Kindlin-2 expression in hepatocytes using the Alb-Cre transgenic mice causes a severe inflammation, resulting in premature death.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, which is supported by survival data and histological analyses shown in the manuscript.

claim: Kindlin-2 loss accelerates hepatocyte apoptosis with subsequent compensatory cell proliferation.
source: Kindlin-2 loss accelerates hepatocyte apoptosis with subsequent compensatory cell proliferation and accumulation of the collagenous extracellular matrix, leading to massive liver fibrosis and dysfunction.
evidence: The abstract states this claim, which is supported by TUNEL staining, Caspase 3 immunohistochemistry, and Ki67 staining data presented in Figure 2.

claim: Kindlin-2 loss leads to accumulation of collagenous extracellular matrix and massive liver fibrosis.
source: Kindlin-2 loss accelerates hepatocyte apoptosis with subsequent compensatory cell proliferation and accumulation of the collagenous extracellular matrix, leading to massive liver fibrosis and dysfunction.
evidence: The abstract states this claim, which is supported by Masson trichrome staining, Sirius red staining, and α-Sma expression data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Kindlin-2 loss abnormally activates the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) pathway.
source: Mechanistically, Kindlin-2 loss abnormally activates the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) pathway.
evidence: The abstract states this mechanism, which is supported by RNA-seq analysis, ELISA measurements of TNFα, and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Blocking TNF signaling by deleting TNF receptor restores liver function and prevents premature death caused by Kindlin-2 loss.
source: Blocking activation of the TNF signaling pathway by deleting TNF receptor or deletion of Caspase 8 expression in hepatocytes essentially restores liver function and prevents premature death caused by Kindlin-2 loss.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by survival curves, serum enzyme measurements, and histological analyses in Figure 5.

claim: Deletion of Caspase 8 expression in hepatocytes restores liver function and prevents premature death caused by Kindlin-2 loss.
source: Blocking activation of the TNF signaling pathway by deleting TNF receptor or deletion of Caspase 8 expression in hepatocytes essentially restores liver function and prevents premature death caused by Kindlin-2 loss.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by survival curves, serum enzyme measurements, and histological analyses in Figure 6.

claim: AAV-mediated overexpression of Kindlin-2 in hepatocytes attenuates D-galactosamine and lipopolysaccharide-induced liver injury and death in mice.
source: Finally, of translational significance, adeno-associated virus mediated overexpression of Kindlin-2 in hepatocytes attenuates the D-galactosamine and lipopolysaccharide-induced liver injury and death in mice.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by survival curves, serum enzyme measurements, and histological analyses in Figure 7.

claim: Kindlin-2 acts as a novel intrinsic inhibitor of the TNF pathway to maintain liver homeostasis.
source: Collectively, we establish that Kindlin-2 acts as a novel intrinsic inhibitor of the TNF pathway to maintain liver homeostasis and may define a useful therapeutic target for liver diseases.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, supported by the collective data from genetic rescue experiments and overexpression studies.

claim: All Kindlin-2 KO mice died at ages between 4 and 5 weeks.
source: Shockingly, all KO mice (>30 mice) died at ages between 4 and 5 weeks (Figure 1a).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 1a which shows the survival curve.

claim: Body weight of KO mice was significantly decreased compared to control littermates at 4 weeks of age.
source: At 4 weeks of age, both body and liver weights of KO mice were slightly, but significantly, decreased compared to those of control littermates (Figure 1b and c).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1b which shows the quantitative data.

claim: Liver weight of KO mice was significantly decreased compared to control littermates at 4 weeks of age.
source: At 4 weeks of age, both body and liver weights of KO mice were slightly, but significantly, decreased compared to those of control littermates (Figure 1b and c).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1c which shows the quantitative data.

claim: Livers from KO mice became coarsened and granular at 4 weeks of age.
source: At this age, livers from KO mice became coarsened and granular (Figure 1d, top panels).
evidence: The text describes this observation and references Figure 1d which shows the gross liver appearance.

claim: Massive ascites was observed in all KO mice but not in control mice.
source: Massive ascites was observed in all KO mice but not in control mice (Figure 1d, bottom panels).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 1d which shows the gross appearance.

claim: KO mice displayed splenomegaly.
source: KO mice displayed a splenomegaly (Figure 1e) and severe cholestasis (Figure 1f).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1e which shows the enlarged spleen.

claim: KO mice displayed severe cholestasis.
source: KO mice displayed a splenomegaly (Figure 1e) and severe cholestasis (Figure 1f).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1f which shows the gallbladder appearance.

claim: Serum from KO mice was more yellowish in color compared to control mice.
source: Compared to serum from control mice, serum from KO mice was more yellowish in color (Figure 1g) and displayed elevated serum levels of both direct and indirect bilirubin (Figure 1h), suggesting that the animals suffered from cholestasis.
evidence: The text describes this observation and references Figure 1g which shows the serum appearance.

claim: KO mice displayed elevated serum levels of both direct and indirect bilirubin.
source: Compared to serum from control mice, serum from KO mice was more yellowish in color (Figure 1g) and displayed elevated serum levels of both direct and indirect bilirubin (Figure 1h), suggesting that the animals suffered from cholestasis.
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1h which shows the quantitative bilirubin measurements.

claim: KO mice suffered from cholestasis.
source: Compared to serum from control mice, serum from KO mice was more yellowish in color (Figure 1g) and displayed elevated serum levels of both direct and indirect bilirubin (Figure 1h), suggesting that the animals suffered from cholestasis.
evidence: The text explicitly states this interpretation based on the yellowish serum and elevated bilirubin levels.

claim: KO mice displayed an osteopenic phenotype with significant reductions in both trabecular and cortical bone volume.
source: KO mice displayed an osteopenic phenotype with significant reductions in both trabecular and cortical bone volume (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1—figure supplement 2 which shows the bone analysis data.

claim: Serum ALT activity was increased in KO mice relative to control mice, starting as early as 2 weeks of age with most dramatic increases at 4 weeks of age.
source: The levels of both serum alanine transaminase (ALT) and aspartate transaminase (AST) activities were increased in KO mice relative to those in control mice, starting as early as 2 weeks of age with most dramatic increases at 4 weeks of age for both enzymes (Figure 1i and j).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1i which shows the ALT measurements over time.

claim: Serum AST activity was increased in KO mice relative to control mice, starting as early as 2 weeks of age with most dramatic increases at 4 weeks of age.
source: The levels of both serum alanine transaminase (ALT) and aspartate transaminase (AST) activities were increased in KO mice relative to those in control mice, starting as early as 2 weeks of age with most dramatic increases at 4 weeks of age for both enzymes (Figure 1i and j).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1j which shows the AST measurements over time.

claim: Serum alkaline phosphatase levels were increased in KO mice relative to control mice.
source: Furthermore, the levels of serum alkaline phosphatase (Figure 1—figure supplement 3a), γ-glutamyl transferase (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b) and total bile acid (Figure 1—figure supplement 3c) were increased in KO mice relative to those in control mice.
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1—figure supplement 3a which shows the data.

claim: Serum γ-glutamyl transferase levels were increased in KO mice relative to control mice.
source: Furthermore, the levels of serum alkaline phosphatase (Figure 1—figure supplement 3a), γ-glutamyl transferase (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b) and total bile acid (Figure 1—figure supplement 3c) were increased in KO mice relative to those in control mice.
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1—figure supplement 3b which shows the data.

claim: Serum total bile acid levels were increased in KO mice relative to control mice.
source: Furthermore, the levels of serum alkaline phosphatase (Figure 1—figure supplement 3a), γ-glutamyl transferase (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b) and total bile acid (Figure 1—figure supplement 3c) were increased in KO mice relative to those in control mice.
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1—figure supplement 3c which shows the data.

claim: Serum protein levels were reduced in KO mice in a time-dependent manner.
source: The levels of serum protein were reduced in a time-dependent manner (Figure 1k).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1k which shows the data over time.

claim: Serum low density lipoprotein level was increased in KO relative to control mice.
source: The level of serum low density lipoprotein was increased and that of serum high density lipoprotein was decreased in KO relative to control mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 3d,e).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1—figure supplement 3d which shows the data.

claim: Serum high density lipoprotein level was decreased in KO relative to control mice.
source: The level of serum low density lipoprotein was increased and that of serum high density lipoprotein was decreased in KO relative to control mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 3d,e).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1—figure supplement 3e which shows the data.

claim: Serum total cholesterol levels were increased in KO versus control mice.
source: The levels of serum total cholesterol (TCH) and ammonia were increased in KO versus control mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 3f,g).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1—figure supplement 3f which shows the data.

claim: Serum ammonia levels were increased in KO versus control mice.
source: The levels of serum total cholesterol (TCH) and ammonia were increased in KO versus control mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 3f,g).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1—figure supplement 3g which shows the data.

claim: Kindlin-2 loss caused massive inflammatory cell infiltration in KO liver, especially in areas surrounding the hepatic sinusoidal vessels.
source: Results from hematoxylin and eosin (H/E) staining of liver sections of 4-week-old control and KO mice revealed that Kindlin-2 loss caused massive inflammatory cell infiltration in KO liver, especially in areas surrounding the hepatic sinusoidal vessels (Figure 1l).
evidence: The text describes this observation from H&E staining and references Figure 1l which shows the histology.

claim: Kindlin-2 loss reduced glycogen accumulation in liver.
source: Kindlin-2 loss reduced the glycogen accumulation, as determined by periodic acid-Schiff staining (Figure 1m) and the mRNA expression levels of liver-related genes, including those encoding glutamine synthetase (Gs), apolipoprotein A-I (Apoa), fibrinogen b (Fbn), and transthyretin (Ttr) (Figure 1n–p).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1m which shows the PAS staining.

claim: Kindlin-2 loss reduced mRNA expression levels of liver-related genes including Gs, Apoa, Fbn, and Ttr.
source: Kindlin-2 loss reduced the glycogen accumulation, as determined by periodic acid-Schiff staining (Figure 1m) and the mRNA expression levels of liver-related genes, including those encoding glutamine synthetase (Gs), apolipoprotein A-I (Apoa), fibrinogen b (Fbn), and transthyretin (Ttr) (Figure 1n–p).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figures 1n-p which show the qRT-PCR data.

claim: Kindlin-2 loss in hepatocytes causes severe liver failure and damages in multiple organs, resulting in premature death.
source: Collectively, these results demonstrate that Kindlin-2 loss in hepatocytes causes a severe liver failure and damages in multiple, resulting in premature death.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the collective data presented in Figure 1 and related supplements.

claim: A progressive increase in hepatocyte apoptosis was observed in KO mice.
source: A progressive increase in hepatocyte apoptosis was observed in KO mice, as demonstrated by TdT-mediated dUTP nick end labeling (TUNEL) staining (Figure 2a and b and Figure 2—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 2a and b which show TUNEL staining and quantification.

claim: Caspase 3 protein immune reactivity was dramatically increased in KO relative to control livers.
source: Consistently, immunohistochemical (IHC) staining showed that the immune reactivity of Caspase 3 protein was dramatically increased in KO relative to control livers (Figure 2c).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 2c which shows the IHC staining.

claim: Levels of both active Caspase 3 and p65 protein were increased in KO livers compared to control livers in a time-dependent manner.
source: The levels of both active Caspase 3 and p65 protein were increased in KO livers compared to those in control livers in a time-dependent manner (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b and c).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 2—figure supplement 1b and c which show the IHC staining over time.

claim: Level of pro-apoptotic Bax protein was time dependently increased in KO livers compared to control livers.
source: Western blotting revealed that level of the pro-apoptotic Bax protein was time dependently increased in KO livers compared to that in control livers (Figure 2d).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 2d which shows the western blot data.

claim: Expression of anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 protein was largely down-regulated in a time-dependent manner by Kindlin-2 deficiency.
source: In contrast, expression of the anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 protein was largely down-regulated in a time-dependent manner by Kindlin-2 deficiency (Figure 2d).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 2d which shows the western blot data.

claim: Levels of Pcna and cyclin D1 proteins were increased in KO livers compared with control livers at 3 and 4 weeks of ages but not at 2 weeks of age.
source: Western blotting showed that the levels of the proliferation cell nuclear antigen (Pcna) and cyclin D1 proteins were increased in KO livers compared with those in control livers at 3 and 4 weeks of ages but not at 2 weeks of age (Figure 2e).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 2e which shows the western blot data over time.

claim: Cell proliferation was increased in KO liver tissue as shown by Ki67 staining.
source: Results from IHC staining of control and KO liver sections using an anti-Ki67 antibody revealed an increase in cell proliferation in KO liver tissue (Figure 2f and g).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 2f and g which show the Ki67 staining and quantification.

claim: Kindlin-2 loss apparently increased the number of cytokeratin 19 (CK19)-expressing biliary/progenitor cells.
source: Kindlin-2 loss apparently increased the number of cytokeratin 19 (CK19)-expressing cells, that is, the biliary/progenitor cells (Figure 2h).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 2h which shows the CK19 staining.

claim: The number of Desmin-expressing hepatic stellate cells was dramatically increased in KO relative to control liver tissues.
source: Immunofluorescence (IF) staining revealed that the number of Desmin-expressing cells, that is, HSC was dramatically increased in KO relative to that in control liver tissues (Figure 2i and j).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 2i and j which show the IF staining and quantification.

claim: A dramatic increase in collagen deposition was observed in livers of 4-week-old KO mice.
source: A dramatic increase in collagen deposition was observed in livers of 4-week-old KO mice, as demonstrated by the Masson trichromatic and Sirius red staining (Figure 3a–d).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 3a-d which show the staining and quantification.

claim: Level of α-smooth muscle actin (α-Sma), a marker for fibrosis, was drastically increased in KO livers in a time-dependent manner.
source: Consistently, results from western blotting revealed that level of α-smooth muscle actin (α-Sma), a marker for fibrosis, was drastically increased in KO livers in a time-dependent manner (Figure 3e).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 3e which shows the western blot data over time.

claim: α-Sma was upregulated in KO mice as shown by IHC staining.
source: IHC staining was also revealed that α-Sma was upregulated in KO mice (Figure 3f).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 3f which shows the IHC staining over time.

claim: mRNA levels of fibrogenic genes including Col1a1, Tgfβ1, Timp1, Acta2, and Col6a1 were up-regulated in KO mice relative to control mice.
source: In addition, the mRNA levels of fibrogenic genes, including those encoding collagen α–1(I) chain (Col1a1), transforming growth factor β1 (Tgfβ1), TIMP metallopeptidase inhibitor 1 (Timp1), actin α2 (Acta2), and collagen type VI, α1 (Col6a1), were up-regulated in KO mice relative to those in control mice (Figure 3g).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 3g which shows the qRT-PCR data.

claim: RNA-seq analyses identified 6746 genes with statistically significant differential expression (3496 up-regulated and 3250 down-regulated genes with log2FC >1.5) between 4-week-old control and KO liver tissues.
source: We further performed RNA-seq analyses from 4-week-old control and KO liver tissues and identified 6746 genes that exhibited statistically significant changes and differential expression (3496 up-regulated genes and 3250 down-regulated genes with log2FC >1.5).
evidence: The text explicitly states the RNA-seq results.

claim: KEGG analysis revealed that Kindlin-2 loss activated TNF signaling pathway, apoptosis, and MAPK pathways in hepatocytes.
source: Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genome (KEGG) analysis revealed that Kindlin-2 loss impacted multiple important pathways. Kindlin-2 loss activated TNF signaling pathway, apoptosis, and MAPK pathways in hepatocytes (Figure 4a and b).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 4a and b which show the KEGG analysis and heatmap.

claim: Serum level of TNFα was dramatically elevated in 4-week-old KO mice compared to control littermates.
source: Consistent with result from the RNA-seq analysis, the serum level of tumor necrosis factor α (Tnfα) was dramatically elevated in 4-week-old KO mice compared to that in control littermates (Figure 4c).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 4c which shows the ELISA data.

claim: mRNA levels of Tnfα were increased in a time-dependent manner in KO livers compared to control livers.
source: Furthermore, the mRNA levels of Tnfα were increased in a time-dependent manner in KO livers compared to those in control livers (Figure 4d).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 4d which shows the qRT-PCR data over time.

claim: Massive macrophage infiltration was observed in KO but not control liver tissues.
source: IHC staining of F4/80 revealed massive macrophage infiltration in KO but not control liver tissues (Figure 4e).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 4e which shows the F4/80 staining.

claim: Expression of CD19 (B cell marker) was increased in KO versus control livers.
source: In addition, the expression of CD19 (B cell marker) and ly6G (neutrophils marker) was increased in KO versus control livers (Figure 4f and g).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 4f which shows the CD19 staining.

claim: Expression of Ly6G (neutrophils marker) was increased in KO versus control livers.
source: In addition, the expression of CD19 (B cell marker) and ly6G (neutrophils marker) was increased in KO versus control livers (Figure 4f and g).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 4g which shows the Ly6G staining.

claim: Numbers of circulating neutrophils, myeloid cells (e.g. monocytes), and blood platelet counts were increased in KO versus control mice.
source: The numbers of circulating neutrophils, myeloid cells (e.g. monocytes), and blood platelet counts were increased in KO versus control mice (Figure 4h–j and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 4h-j and Figure 4—figure supplement 1 which show the complete blood count data.

claim: Kindlin-2 knockdown by shRNA dramatically reduced Fermt2 mRNA and Kindlin-2 protein levels in Huh7 cells.
source: The levels of Fermt2 mRNA and Kindlin-2 protein were dramatically reduced by Fermt2 shRNA (sh-K2) in both Huh7 (Figure 4k and l) and HepG2 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2a,b).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 4k and l which show the qRT-PCR and western blot data.

claim: Kindlin-2 knockdown by shRNA dramatically reduced Fermt2 mRNA and Kindlin-2 protein levels in HepG2 cells.
source: The levels of Fermt2 mRNA and Kindlin-2 protein were dramatically reduced by Fermt2 shRNA (sh-K2) in both Huh7 (Figure 4k and l) and HepG2 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2a,b).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 4—figure supplement 2a,b which show the qRT-PCR and western blot data.

claim: mRNA levels of Tnfα and Birc3 were up-regulated by Kindlin-2 knockdown in Huh7 cells.
source: The mRNA levels of Tnfα and Birc3 (Baculoviral IAP repeat containing 3) were up-regulated by Kindlin-2 knockdown in Huh7 (Figure 4m) and HepG2 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 4m which shows the qRT-PCR data.

claim: mRNA levels of Tnfα and Birc3 were up-regulated by Kindlin-2 knockdown in HepG2 cells.
source: The mRNA levels of Tnfα and Birc3 (Baculoviral IAP repeat containing 3) were up-regulated by Kindlin-2 knockdown in Huh7 (Figure 4m) and HepG2 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 4—figure supplement 2c which shows the qRT-PCR data.

claim: TNF protein level was dramatically increased in supernatants of sh-K2 Huh7 cultures.
source: ELISA showed a dramatic increase in TNF protein in supernatants of the sh-K2 Huh7 (Figure 4n) and HepG2 cultures (Figure 4—figure supplement 2d).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 4n which shows the ELISA data.

claim: TNF protein level was dramatically increased in supernatants of sh-K2 HepG2 cultures.
source: ELISA showed a dramatic increase in TNF protein in supernatants of the sh-K2 Huh7 (Figure 4n) and HepG2 cultures (Figure 4—figure supplement 2d).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 4—figure supplement 2d which shows the ELISA data.

claim: Kindlin-2 loss impaired focal adhesion formation and caused reduced tension in hepatocytes.
source: Results from F-actin IF staining showed that Kindlin-2 loss impaired the FA formation and caused a reduced tension (Figure 4o).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 4o which shows the IF staining.

claim: Deletion of Kindlin-2 in hepatocyte resulted in defects in cell spreading and attachment.
source: Moreover, deletion of Kindlin-2 in hepatocyte resulted in defects in cell spreading and attachment (Figure 4p).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 4p which shows the cell spreading images.

claim: Ablation of Kindlin-2 in hepatocyte resulted in upregulation of TNF signaling pathway.
source: Collectively, these results illustrate that ablation of Kindlin-2 in hepatocyte resulted in upregulation of TNF signaling pathway.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the collective in vitro and in vivo data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Deletion of Tnfr genes completely prevented the premature death of Kindlin-2 KO mice.
source: Strikingly, deletion of Tnfr genes completely prevented the premature death of the Kindlin-2 KO mice. In contrast to the fact that all Kindlin-2 KO mice died between 4 and 5 weeks of ages, no KO/Tnfr-/- mice (>30 mice) died during this period of time and beyond (Figure 5a).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 5a which shows the survival curves.

claim: Serum ALT levels were significantly lower in KO/Tnfr-/- mice than in Kindlin-2 KO mice.
source: The levels of serum ALT and AST were significantly lower in KO/Tnfr-/- mice than in Kindlin-2 KO mice (Figure 5b and c).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 5b which shows the ALT data.

claim: Serum AST levels were significantly lower in KO/Tnfr-/- mice than in Kindlin-2 KO mice.
source: The levels of serum ALT and AST were significantly lower in KO/Tnfr-/- mice than in Kindlin-2 KO mice (Figure 5b and c).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 5c which shows the AST data.

claim: Deletion of Tnfr genes rescued the liver damage in Kindlin-2 KO mice.
source: As shown in Figure 5d, deletion of Tnfr genes rescued the liver damage in Kindlin-2 KO mice.
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 5d which shows the H&E staining.

claim: Increases in collagen deposition, macrophage infiltration, cell proliferation, fibrosis, and apoptosis caused by Kindlin-2 deficiency were markedly reversed by Tnfr genes deletion.
source: The increases in collagen deposition, macrophage infiltration, cell proliferation, fibrosis, and apoptosis caused by Kindlin-2 deficiency were markedly reversed by Tnfr genes deletion (Figure 5e–n).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 5e-n which show various histological and molecular analyses.

claim: Deletion of Caspase 8 in hepatocytes essentially prevented premature death of Kindlin-2 KO mice.
source: Shockingly, deletion of Caspase 8 in hepatocytes essentially prevented premature death of Kindlin-2 KO mice (Figure 6a).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 6a which shows the survival curves.

claim: Serum ALT levels were significantly lower in KO/Casp8-/- mice than in Kindlin-2 KO mice.
source: The levels of serum ALT and AST were significantly lower in KO/Casp8-/- mice than in Kindlin-2 KO mice (Figure 6b and c).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 6b which shows the ALT data.

claim: Serum AST levels were significantly lower in KO/Casp8-/- mice than in Kindlin-2 KO mice.
source: The levels of serum ALT and AST were significantly lower in KO/Casp8-/- mice than in Kindlin-2 KO mice (Figure 6b and c).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 6c which shows the AST data.

claim: Deletion of Caspase 8 restored the liver damage in Kindlin-2 KO mice.
source: Deletion of Caspase 8 restored the liver damage in Kindlin-2 KO mice (Figure 6d).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 6d which shows the H&E staining.

claim: Increases in macrophage infiltration, cell proliferation, fibrosis, and apoptosis caused by Kindlin-2 deficiency were markedly attenuated by Caspase 8 deletion.
source: The increases in macrophage infiltration, cell proliferation, fibrosis, and apoptosis caused by Kindlin-2 deficiency were markedly attenuated by Caspase 8 deletion (Figure 6e–l).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 6e-l which show various histological and molecular analyses.

claim: GalN/LPS administration caused a dramatic decrease in Kindlin-2 accumulation in liver tissues of C57BL/6 mice.
source: Immunoblotting analysis detected a dramatic decrease in Kindlin-2 accumulation in the liver tissues of C57BL/6 after administration with GalN/LPS (Figure 7a and b).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 7a and b which show the western blot and quantification.

claim: Kindlin-2 protein level was markedly increased in livers of mice injected with AAV8-K2.
source: The level of Kindlin-2 protein was markedly increased in livers of mice injected with AAV8-K2 (Figure 7d and e).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 7d and e which show the western blot and quantification.

claim: GalN/LPS resulted in acute death of all mice around 14-15 hr of treatment.
source: As expected, GalN/LPS resulted in acute death of all mice around 14–15 hr of the treatment.
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation.

claim: Kindlin-2 overexpression significantly extended the life span of mice compared with control mice injected with AAV8-GFP after GalN/LPS treatment.
source: Kindlin-2 overexpression (OE) significantly extended the life span of mice compared with control mice injected with AAV8-GFP (Figure 7f).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 7f which shows the survival curve.

claim: Kindlin-2 overexpression improved the gross liver appearance in GalN/LPS-treated mice.
source: Kindlin-2 OE improved the gross liver appearance in GalN/LPS-treated mice (Figure 7g).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 7g which shows the gross liver images.

claim: Kindlin-2 overexpression significantly decreased the levels of serum ALT in GalN/LPS-treated mice.
source: Kindlin-2 OE significantly decreased the levels of serum ALT and AST in GalN/LPS-treated mice (Figure 7h and i), but no difference in untreated Kindlin-2 OE and control mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 7h which shows the ALT data.

claim: Kindlin-2 overexpression significantly decreased the levels of serum AST in GalN/LPS-treated mice.
source: Kindlin-2 OE significantly decreased the levels of serum ALT and AST in GalN/LPS-treated mice (Figure 7h and i), but no difference in untreated Kindlin-2 OE and control mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 7i which shows the AST data.

claim: Histological damages in liver caused by GalN/LPS were markedly ameliorated by Kindlin-2 overexpression.
source: Results from H/E staining revealed that histological damages in liver caused by GalN/LPS were markedly ameliorated by Kindlin-2 OE (Figure 7j).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 7j which shows the H&E staining.

claim: Kindlin-2 overexpression decreased GalN/LPS-induced hepatocyte apoptosis as measured by IHC staining of Caspase-3 and TUNEL staining.
source: Furthermore, Kindlin-2 OE decreased GalN/LPS-induced hepatocyte apoptosis, as measured by IHC staining of Caspase-3 and TUNEL staining of liver sections (Figure 7k–m).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 7k-m which show the Caspase-3 IHC and TUNEL staining.

claim: Inflammatory liver diseases are a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide.
source: Inflammatory liver diseases are a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide; however, underlying mechanisms are incompletely understood.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that reflects established knowledge in the field.

claim: Underlying mechanisms of inflammatory liver diseases are incompletely understood.
source: Inflammatory liver diseases are a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide; however, underlying mechanisms are incompletely understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The liver is a multifunctional organ that plays critical roles in regulation of metabolism and detoxification and maintenance of whole-body homeostasis.
source: The liver is a multifunctional organ that plays critical roles in regulation of metabolism and detoxification and maintenance of the whole-body homeostasis (Jones et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a general statement about liver function supported by a citation.

claim: Liver comprises parenchymal cells and non-parenchymal cells.
source: Liver comprised parenchymal cells and non-parenchymal cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Parenchymal cells include hepatocytes and endothelial cells.
source: The former includes hepatocytes and endothelial cells; the latter includes hepatic stellate cells (HSC) and Kupffer cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Non-parenchymal cells include hepatic stellate cells (HSC) and Kupffer cells.
source: The former includes hepatocytes and endothelial cells; the latter includes hepatic stellate cells (HSC) and Kupffer cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established anatomical knowledge.

claim: Abnormal activation of TNF signaling stimulates inflammation and apoptosis, which are intertwined during development and progression of liver diseases.
source: Abnormal activation of the TNF signaling stimulates inflammation and apoptosis, which are intertwined during the development and progression of liver diseases (Guicciardi and Gores, 2005; Tacke and Zimmermann, 2014; Garcia-Martinez et al., 2016; Schuppan et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: TNFα exerts its actions through binding and activating two different types of receptors, TNFR1 and TNFR2.
source: TNFα exerts its actions through binding and activating two different types of receptors, TNF receptor 1 (TNFR1) and TNFR2 (Wajant and Siegmund, 2019).
